params.body:
## Why

Shane, 19 September 2026: the findings should say which pull request ended them, and open findings should be triageable on GitHub instead of only in the repository. The catch is that a second place which claims to be the truth drifts within a week, so the direction is one way: the file is the source, the issue is the workbench.

## From a finding to the code that ended it

- A resolved finding carries `opgelost_in: #<pull request>`. `RulesIdentityTest` requires it for anything resolved from today on, and refuses the field on a finding that is not resolved.
- The 164 findings resolved before today are filled in from the git history: for each file, the merge commit that carried its last change names the pull request. Every one of them resolved (none unknown), so the way from complaint to code is complete for the whole cutover period.
- `CLAUDE.md` says what a pull request that ends a finding writes.

## The mirror on GitHub

- `bin/findings-to-issues`: without arguments it says what it would open (one line per finding, with its labels), `--apply` opens them, `--gh` uses the operator's own `gh`, `--ernst=nu` narrows to a severity.
- Through the control gateway by default: kind `issue.open` (control v0.28.0, abovebeyond-ai/control#85, in the grant since abovebeyond-ai/elixir#222 and in the capability since abovebeyond-ai/portal#333), so an issue a session opens carries a record like a branch and a pull request do. `hand.mjs issue` is the client side.
- The issue body is the finding's prose plus a small table (ernst, regel, beslist, gevonden, waar) and the path of the file that is the source. Labels: `bevinding`, the severity, and `beslist: <naam>`.
- The number comes back into the file as `issue: <n>`; the pull request that fixes the finding closes the issue with "Fixes #n". Closing is never this script's work.
- `bin/findings-issues.php` holds the logic, beside the existing `bin/rules-findings.php`; no Laravel, no YAML library, same parsing as the rest.

## Tests

`FindingsIssuesTest` (6): the body carries the facts and names the file as the source, the labels say what it is and who decides (and an invented severity becomes no label), only open findings without an issue are mirrored, a resolved finding with an issue is reported for closing, the number lands in the frontmatter without touching the prose and replaces itself on a second write, and every finding in the repository renders. `RulesIdentityTest` gained the three guards. Run: `FindingsIssuesTest|Rules*` → 27 tests, 876 assertions. `php bin/rules-sources`: Geen problemen.

## Next

88 findings are open and have no issue yet; `bin/findings-to-issues --apply` opens them in one run. Worth doing per severity, `--ernst=nu` first, so the list stays readable.
params.title: From a finding to the pull request that ended it, and a mirror on GitHub
